response.justification: The candidate is an experienced senior engineer (15+ years) with strong breadth, distributed-systems exposure, and a genuine track record in low-latency, event-driven services — but almost entirely in web/backend stacks (TypeScript, Node.js, D, Ember/React). The role's core requirement is deep, current C++/STL expertise for industrial automation, and the resume shows only ~6 months of C/C++ work at National Instruments in 2014–2015 plus a university thesis project; C++ is not even listed among current skills. There is no evidence of IEC 62443/SDL secure-engineering practice, MQTT/industrial protocols, or industrial automation domain experience, which are central rather than peripheral to this position. Strong general engineering ability does not offset a mismatch on the primary technical axis.
strengths: Deep experience with high-throughput, low-latency, event-driven distributed systems
Strong software craftsmanship: TDD, CI/CD, testing tooling, mentoring and public workshops
Broad polyglot background with proven ability to pick up new stacks and ship end-to-end
concerns: Minimal and dated C++/STL experience (~6 months, 2014–2015); not a listed current skill
No demonstrated IEC 62443, SDL, or industrial cybersecurity background
No industrial automation, MQTT, OPC UA, or Modbus/IEC protocol exposure

key_factors.factor: Industrial automation and security standards (IEC 62443/SDL) gap
